scope: cross-version migration path (CrossVersionMigrator + StableStaker migration surface)
echidnaNote: Medusa (primary) ran successfully, so Echidna was not needed; echidna is not installed on this host.

honesty.claim: NO COUNTEREXAMPLE FOUND in 750,000 Foundry calls (1,500 sequences of depth 500) and 1,003,230 Medusa calls (10,029 sequences), plus 42,000 stateless fuzz runs. This is absence of evidence, not proof. Only Halmos [PASS] would be a proof; these are bug-finding runs.
honesty.notVacuous: Every run seeds real stakes across 2 tokens and 2 decimals, a wired below-par source strategy, a wired haircut-capable destination strategy, non-zero elapsed time, an executed initiateMigration and an executed non-empty migrate; the last Foundry run alone completed 22 migration epochs, 43 non-empty migrate() batches and 24 self-exits, moved 44.6e9 token wei of principal and minted 1.34e25 phUSD. afterInvariant() would have failed the run loudly had any of that been zero.
honesty.sensitivityProven: Two deliberate mutants were injected and both were caught: (a) asserting the migrator's ABSOLUTE balance is zero (fails under donations), (b) comparing per-user delivered value against reference+1 in the order-independence fuzz. A third canary (assert ghost_revivals == 0) was tripped by Medusa, proving the epoch-revival path is genuinely reached.

invariantOutcomes.name: invariant_01_migratorTokenConservation
invariantOutcomes.notes: Per-call balance delta was zero on every one of the observed migrate() calls, and the residual allowance to the destination staker was zero after every call. Attacked with fuzzed batch composition/order, duplicate entries, already-migrated addresses and direct donations to the migrator (donations make the absolute balance non-zero without ever breaking the delta identity).

invariantOutcomes.name: invariant_02_noOverMintAcrossTheHop
invariantOutcomes.notes: Checked against BOTH a loose cap (sum of rates * wall clock) and a tight cap counting only intervals in which a pool was Active AND held principal. In the final run 1.34e25 phUSD was minted against a tight cap of 3.74e25 - the gap is unclaimed accrual, not slack in the invariant.

invariantOutcomes.name: invariant_03_noDoubleCredit
invariantOutcomes.notes: No user ever held a position on both stakers, and no destination credit ever exceeded the frozen source snapshot credit. Checked over every cohort of every epoch, not just the current one.

invariantOutcomes.name: testFuzz_04_creditIsOrderAndCompositionIndependent
invariantOutcomes.notes: 20,000 fuzz runs. Two scenarios executed from the same EVM state (vm.snapshotState/vm.revertToState): one canonical all-users batch vs a fuzzed partition into 1-6 batches in a fuzzed permutation with a fuzzed subset self-exiting first. Delivered value matched to the wei in every run, across source realization factors from 50% to 100% of par.

invariantOutcomes.name: invariant_05_solvency
invariantOutcomes.notes: Per-epoch credits never exceeded that epoch's R, and lifetime credits never exceeded the sum of every epoch's R (44.6e9 paid against 46.5e9 realized in the final run - the difference is floor-division dust retained by the protocol).

notMeaningfullyExercised: The zero-credit batch-kill path was NOT reached inside the stateful campaign (ghost_zeroCreditReverts == 0 in every run): the seeded cohort principals are far above the dust window, and a randomly-fuzzed batch essentially never produces a source credit that lands in the 1-wei poison band. That path is instead covered exhaustively by the dedicated DustPoison fuzz tests.
Fee-on-transfer and rebasing tokens were not modelled (C4 known-invalid, and the profiler already showed the migrate() flow reverts atomically under them).
Reentrancy via an ERC777-style token hook (profile item CVM-U1) was NOT modelled - the tokens used are plain ERC20s with no callbacks.

newFinding.title: setYieldStrategy sweeps unmatched idle balance into the strategy, permanently bricking that pool's initiateMigration ("incomplete exit")
newFinding.discoveredBy: Tier-3 stateful invariant campaign (repeated migration epochs)
newFinding.pocResult: 5/5 tests pass, including one against the REAL ERC4626YieldStrategy
newFinding.summary: setYieldStrategy (:271-274) deposits the contract's ENTIRE idle token balance into the newly wired strategy while the empty-pool gate forces totalStaked == 0, and nothing raises totalStaked to match. The wiring therefore leaves strategy.principalOf(token, staker) == totalStaked + idleAtWiringTime permanently. initiateMigration requests exactly P = totalStaked and then post-checks require(strategy.principalOf(...) == 0, 'StableStaker: incomplete exit') (:461-464): the swept surplus is never requested, so the post-check can never pass and the pool's terminal-migration path is dead for the lifetime of that wiring. The in-place drain branch cannot recover it either, because it is capped at totalStaked, which the empty-pool gate pins to 0.
triggers: NO ATTACKER - the protocol's own documented revival runbook. A completed migration leaves floor-division dust idle in the staker; the runbook (initiateMigration -> batchMigrate -> finalizeAndReset -> setYieldStrategy) sweeps that dust, so the revived pool can never be migrated again. The invariant campaign observed 62 wei of such dust over 21 revivals.
A permissionless 1-wei transfer to the staker front-running the owner's setYieldStrategy transaction.
newFinding.impact: The terminal-migration path - the protocol's only ordered, loss-socializing exit and its only cross-version hop - becomes unavailable for that pool. If the strategy later goes underwater, withdraw is blocked by the underwater guard and initiateMigration reverts, leaving only the FCFS emergencyWithdraw escape hatch, which is exactly the socialization failure the (R,P) snapshot exists to prevent. No direct theft; recovery requires every user to exit and the pool to be re-wired (which orphans the swept principal inside the abandoned strategy).
newFinding.mitigation: Either rescue the idle balance before wiring (proved to work in the PoC), or make setYieldStrategy sweep nothing on an empty pool, or relax the initiateMigration post-check to require principalOf <= tolerated surplus / request the full client principal rather than P.

dustPoisonQuantification.question: How wide is the dust-poison window that code-scanner PoC'd, honestly claimed as 'single-digit wei'?
dustPoisonQuantification.verdict: CORROBORATED, and now given a closed form. The claim stands; severity should NOT be raised.
dustPoisonQuantification.mechanism: The batch dies when depositFor(token, user, d) reverts for a source credit d > 0. The migrator's `if (amounts[i] > 0)` skip tests the SOURCE credit, so it never fires.

measuredWindows.closedForm: window == ceil(sharePrice) - 1 wei above par (1 wei just below par, 0 exactly at par)
measuredWindows.fuzzAssertion: 2,000 fuzz runs over share prices in [0.5x, 10x] par: window <= 9 wei in every run.

dustPoisonQuantification.refinement: The poison quantity is the DESTINATION-side credit, not the residual principal. An underwater source (R < P) scales credits DOWN, so a 1-wei residual floors to credit 0 and is safely skipped, while the poisoning residual principal moves up to roughly window * P/S. 20,000 fuzz runs over source realization 20%-100% and residuals 1-4000 wei confirmed the batch reverts EXACTLY when the credit lands in the window and never otherwise.
dustPoisonQuantification.conclusion: Materially wider than single-digit wei only for an absurd destination share price (>= 10 assets per share) or a >90% deposit haircut. Neither is a realistic stable-vault configuration, so the Low rating is corroborated rather than raised.
